## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose
This document provides a detailed description of the Software Requirements Specification (SRS) for the Regional Traffic Management and Data Exchange System (RTMDES). It is intended for stakeholders, including project managers, system architects, developers, and testers, and serves as a contract on the system's required capabilities.

### 1.2 Project Scope
The RTMDES will provide a regional traffic data repository and communication infrastructure to connect existing Traffic Management Centers (TMCs) across the Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex. The system will enable the standardized exchange of traffic data and device control between multiple agencies using established Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) standards.

**In-Scope:**
*   Centralized aggregation of roadway, incident, and device status data.
*   Web-based visualization and reporting tools for authorized users.
*   Remote control of compliant ITS field devices.
*   Multi-agency data sharing and interoperability via standardized interfaces.

**Out-of-Scope:**
*   Direct, real-time control of individual traffic signals.
*   Provision of real-time navigation services to the public or vehicles.
*   Construction or deployment of new physical traffic infrastructure.

### 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations

| Acronym | Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| **C2C** | Center-to-Center |
| **CCTV** | Closed-Circuit Television |
| **DMS** | Dynamic Message Sign |
| **GUI** | Graphical User Interface |
| **HAR** | Highway Advisory Radio |
| **ITS** | Intelligent Transportation Systems |
| **LCS** | Lane Control Signal |
| **RTMDES** | Regional Traffic Management and Data Exchange System |
| **TMC** | Traffic Management Center |
| **TMDD** | Traffic Management Data Dictionary (ITS Standard) |
| **TxDOT** | Texas Department of Transportation |

### 1.4 References
*   ITS Standards - Traffic Management Data Dictionary (TMDD)
*   ITS Standards - DATEX/ASN
*   TxDOT C2C Project Documentation

## 2. Overall Description

### 2.1 Product Perspective
The RTMDES serves as a regional extension of the TxDOT Center-to-Center (C2C) project. It acts as a middleware layer, integrating with existing TMCs and their ITS field devices (e.g., DMS, CCTV, ramp meters) via standardized interfaces. This system is designed to be a reusable foundation for future statewide traffic management system expansions.

### 2.2 Product Functions
The core functions of the system are:
1.  **Data Aggregation:** Collect and store traffic data from multiple, disparate TMCs.
2.  **Data Visualization:** Present aggregated data via an interactive web-based map.
3.  **Incident Management:** Facilitate the reporting and management of incidents and lane closures.
4.  **Device Control:** Allow authorized users to remotely control ITS devices across agency boundaries.
5.  **Status Monitoring:** Provide real-time monitoring of the status of network devices and field equipment.
6.  **Data Sharing:** Enable secure and standardized data exchange between all connected agencies.

### 2.3 User Characteristics

| User Class | Description | Key Tasks |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Agency Operator** | Personnel from traffic agencies without a formal TMC. | View traffic conditions and incidents via the web map. Report new incidents and lane closures. |
| **TMC Operator** | Personnel from regional TMCs with advanced privileges. | All tasks of an Agency Operator. Remotely control ITS devices (DMS, CCTV, etc.). Monitor real-time device status. |
| **System Administrator** | Technical staff responsible for system health and user management. | Manage user accounts and permissions. Monitor system performance and logs. |

### 2.4 Constraints
1.  **Technical:** All data exchange with external TMCs must comply with ITS standards (TMDD, DATEX/ASN).
2.  **Implementation:** No custom protocols shall be developed for new ITS-compliant systems; existing standards must be used.
3.  **Regulatory:** The system must adhere to data sharing agreements and security policies of all participating agencies.

### 2.5 Assumptions and Dependencies
*   **Dependencies:**
    *   All connected TMCs must adopt and provide data feeds using the specified ITS standards (TMDD).
    *   The underlying network infrastructure must support reliable TCP/IP communications.
*   **Assumptions:**
    *   Existing TMCs have the capability to generate and transmit standardized data feeds.
    *   Sufficient network bandwidth is available to handle real-time data and device control commands.

## 3. System Features

### 3.1 Centralized Data Repository
**Description:** The system shall maintain a centralized database for regional traffic data.
**Requirements:**
*   `REQ-DR-001`: The system shall aggregate and store roadway data (e.g., volume, speed, occupancy) from all connected TMCs.
*   `REQ-DR-002`: The system shall aggregate and store incident data (e.g., type, location, severity) from all connected TMCs and internal reports.
*   `REQ-DR-003`: The system shall aggregate and store the status of all known ITS field devices (e.g., operational, faulty, communication status).

### 3.2 Web-Based Map Visualization
**Description:** The system shall provide a web-based graphical user interface (GUI) for visualizing regional traffic data.
**Requirements:**
*   `REQ-MAP-001`: The GUI shall display an interactive map of the Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex road network.
*   `REQ-MAP-002`: The map shall visually represent real-time traffic conditions (e.g., using color-coded segments for congestion levels).
*   `REQ-MAP-003`: The map shall display icons for active incidents, lane closures, and the locations of ITS devices.
*   `REQ-MAP-004`: Users shall be able to filter the displayed data by type (e.g., show only incidents, hide all DMS).

### 3.3 Incident and Lane Closure Management
**Description:** The system shall provide a GUI for authorized users to report and manage traffic incidents and lane closures.
**Requirements:**
*   `REQ-IM-001`: Authorized users shall be able to create a new incident report, including type, location, description, and time.
*   `REQ-IM-002`: The system shall broadcast new incident reports to all connected TMCs per TMDD standards.
*   `REQ-IM-003`: Authorized users shall be able to update the status of an incident (e.g., verified, cleared).
*   `REQ-IM-004`: The system shall provide equivalent functionality for the management of planned and unplanned lane closures.

### 3.4 Remote ITS Device Control
**Description:** The system shall allow authorized TMC Operators to remotely control ITS devices that are owned by other connected agencies.
**Requirements:**
*   `REQ-CTRL-001`: The system shall provide a GUI for TMC Operators to send control commands to Dynamic Message Signs (DMS).
*   `REQ-CTRL-002`: The system shall provide a GUI for TMC Operators to control pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) functions of CCTV cameras.
*   `REQ-CTRL-003`: The system shall provide interfaces for controlling Lane Control Signals (LCS), ramp meters, and Highway Advisory Radio (HAR) systems.
*   `REQ-CTRL-004`: All control commands shall be routed through the owning TMC's system using standardized protocols.

### 3.5 Real-Time Device Status Monitoring
**Description:** The system shall monitor and display the operational status of network devices and field equipment.
**Requirements:**
*   `REQ-MON-001`: The system shall provide a dashboard or status panel indicating the communication health of connected TMCs.
*   `REQ-MON-002`: The system shall display the operational status (e.g., online, offline, fault) of individual field devices like DMS and CCTV.
*   `REQ-MON-003`: The system shall generate alerts for system administrators when a TMC feed is lost or a critical field device fails.

## 4. External Interface Requirements

### 4.1 User Interfaces
*   **Web Map GUI:** A responsive, browser-based interface for data visualization and incident reporting.
*   **Remote Control GUI:** A secure, role-based interface for TMC Operators to control field devices.
*   **Admin Dashboard:** A web-based portal for system administration and monitoring.

### 4.2 Hardware Interfaces
The system shall interface indirectly with the following hardware via connected TMCs:
*   Dynamic Message Signs (DMS)
*   CCTV Camera Systems
*   Traffic Signal Controllers
*   Ramp Metering Systems
*   Vehicle Detection Sensors (e.g., loops, radar)

### 4.3 Software Interfaces
*   **SI-1: TMC Data Feeds:** Interface with external TMC systems to receive standardized data (TMDD/DATEX) over TCP/IP.
*   **SI-2: TMC Control Gateway:** Interface with external TMC systems to send device control commands using standardized protocols.

### 4.4 Communication Interfaces
*   All C2C communications shall use TCP/IP over the designated regional network.
*   Data exchange formats shall be TMDD (primarily) and DATEX/ASN.

## 5. Non-Functional Requirements

### 5.1 Performance Requirements
*   `REQ-PERF-001`: The data repository shall be capable of ingesting and processing data feeds from up to 20 concurrent TMCs.
*   `REQ-PERF-002`: The web map shall update traffic condition and incident data with a maximum latency of 60 seconds from the time of source data receipt.
*   `REQ-PERF-003`: Device control commands shall be delivered to the target TMC with a maximum latency of 10 seconds.

### 5.2 Availability Requirements
*   `REQ-AVL-001`: The system shall be available for traffic operations 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with an uptime of 99.5%.
*   `REQ-AVL-002`: Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed 4 hours per month and must be communicated 72 hours in advance.

### 5.3 Security Requirements
*   `REQ-SEC-001`: The system shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) to enforce data access and device control permissions.
*   `REQ-SEC-002`: All user sessions shall be authenticated and encrypted (HTTPS).
*   `REQ-SEC-003`: Data in transit between TMCs and the central repository shall be encrypted.

### 5.4 Interoperability Requirements
*   `REQ-INT-001`: The system shall exclusively use ITS standards (TMDD) for all data exchange to ensure interoperability with existing and future TMCs.

### 5.5 Operational Modes
*   **Normal Mode:** The system performs all data aggregation, visualization, and control functions.
*   **Test Mode:** The system logs all incoming and outgoing data transactions for validation and debugging but does not execute live device control commands.

---
## 6. Acceptance Criteria
The system will be considered acceptable upon successful completion of User Acceptance Testing (UAT) demonstrating:
1.  Operation in **Normal Mode** for a continuous 72-hour period without critical failures.
2.  Successful exchange of all specified data types (roadway, incident, device status) with all participating TMCs per TMDD standards.
3.  Full functionality of the web-based map visualization and incident reporting GUI.
4.  Verified remote control of at least one device type from each major category (DMS, CCTV, Ramp Meter) through the interface of a connected TMC.

- Integration capabilities with existing weather data sources

This document specifies the requirements for a free, open-source PDF manipulation tool that provides both graphical user interface (GUI) and console-based functionality. The software enables users to perform various PDF manipulation operations without commercial cost or licensing restrictions.

The system provides comprehensive PDF manipulation capabilities including splitting, merging, rotating, and visual reordering of PDF documents. The tool is designed to be platform-independent and accessible to both technical and non-technical users.

- PDF splitting by multiple criteria
- PDF merging and extraction

## 1 Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose
This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document describes the functional and non-functional requirements for the Tarrant County Indigent Defense Management System (IDMS). The system will manage court-appointed defense services for indigent defendants in Tarrant County, Texas, ensuring compliance with Texas legal requirements while streamlining defense coordination processes.

### 1.2 Scope
The IDMS shall provide comprehensive management of court-appointed defense services including:

**In-Scope:**
- Request submission for court-appointed counsel
- Attorney appointment processing and tracking
- Defendant-attorney contact tracking and reporting
- Case filing coordination with District Attorney
- Court scheduling and management
- Attorney compensation request processing
- Attorney appointment rotation list management
- Texas Fair Defense Act compliance reporting

**Out-of-Scope:**
- Financial management beyond attorney payment processing
- Case disposition tracking and management
- Legal representation decision-making
- Comprehensive accounting system functionality

## 2 Overall Description

### 2.1 Product Perspective
The IDMS is a component of Tarrant County's Integrated Justice Information System (IJIS) initiative. The system replaces manual processes for indigent defense coordination and integrates with existing county justice systems to enable seamless data flow across agencies.

### 2.2 Product Functions
The system shall provide the following core functionalities:

1. **Counsel Request Management** - Submit and process requests for court-appointed counsel
2. **Appointment Processing** - Manage attorney assignments and rotation lists
3. **Contact Tracking** - Monitor and report defendant-attorney contacts
4. **Case Coordination** - Coordinate with District Attorney on case filings
5. **Court Scheduling** - Manage court settings and appearances
6. **Compensation Processing** - Handle attorney payment requests and approvals
7. **Compliance Reporting** - Generate reports required by Texas Fair Defense Act

### 2.3 User Characteristics

| User Role | Responsibilities | Technical Proficiency |
|-----------|------------------|----------------------|
| Office of Attorney Appointments Staff | Manage counsel requests, appointments, compensation | Intermediate computer skills |
| Defense Attorneys | Submit contact logs, request payments, update availability | Basic to intermediate computer skills |
| Magistrates/Court Coordinators | Submit indigency requests, set court dates, confirm status | Intermediate computer skills |
| District Attorney Staff | File charges, notify case decisions | Intermediate computer skills |

### 2.4 Operating Environment
- **Platform**: Web-based application accessible via county network
- **Integration**: Must interface with Court Case Management System and DA Electronic Filing System
- **Security**: Must comply with Texas DITR security standards
- **Browser Support**: Current versions of major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge)

### 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
- Must comply with Texas UETA and DITR guidelines for electronic transactions
- Must integrate with existing Court Case Management System architecture
- Must adhere to Texas Code of Criminal Procedure requirements
- Must maintain data consistency with external justice systems

## 3 System Features

### 3.1 Counsel Request Management

#### 3.1.1 Description
The system shall process requests for court-appointed counsel submitted by magistrates and court coordinators, ensuring all requests are processed within 24 hours of submission.

#### 3.1.2 Functional Requirements

**FR-001: Request Submission**
```markdown
- **Priority**: High
- **Description**: Magistrates shall be able to submit indigency requests electronically
- **Inputs**: Defendant information, case details, indigency determination
- **Processing**: Validate required fields, assign unique case identifier
- **Outputs**: Confirmed request with tracking number, system timestamp
```

**FR-002: Request Processing**
```markdown
- **Priority**: High
- **Description**: OAA staff shall process requests and assign attorneys within 24 hours
- **Inputs**: Request details, attorney availability, rotation list
- **Processing**: Check attorney rotation, assign qualified attorney, notify parties
- **Outputs**: Attorney assignment, notification to all parties, status update
```

### 3.2 Attorney Appointment and Contact Tracking

#### 3.2.1 Description
The system shall manage attorney appointments and track initial contact with defendants, ensuring contact occurs within one working day of appointment.

#### 3.2.2 Functional Requirements

**FR-010: Appointment Management**
```markdown
- **Priority**: High
- **Description**: Maintain and update attorney appointment rotation lists
- **Inputs**: Attorney qualifications, availability, case types
- **Processing**: Rotate assignments based on established criteria and availability
- **Outputs**: Updated rotation lists, assignment records
```

**FR-011: Contact Tracking**
```markdown
- **Priority**: High
- **Description**: Track and confirm first attorney-defendant contact
- **Inputs**: Contact date/time, method, outcome
- **Processing**: Validate contact occurs within 1 working day, flag exceptions
- **Outputs**: Contact confirmation, exception reports
```

### 3.3 Case Filing Coordination

#### 3.3.1 Description
The system shall coordinate case filing decisions with the District Attorney's office and manage related communications.

#### 3.3.2 Functional Requirements

**FR-020: DA Coordination**
```markdown
- **Priority**: Medium
- **Description**: Facilitate communication with DA regarding charge filings
- **Inputs**: Case information, filing decisions, charge details
- **Processing**: Route information to appropriate parties, track responses
- **Outputs**: Case status updates, notification records
```

### 3.4 Court Scheduling Management

#### 3.4.1 Description
The system shall manage court settings and appearances for defendants with appointed counsel.

#### 3.4.2 Functional Requirements

**FR-030: Scheduling Management**
```markdown
- **Priority**: Medium
- **Description**: Schedule and track court appearances and settings
- **Inputs**: Court dates, appearance types, participant availability
- **Processing**: Check conflicts, send notifications, track attendance
- **Outputs**: Court calendars, appearance records, notification logs
```

### 3.5 Compensation Processing

#### 3.5.1 Description
The system shall process attorney compensation requests and approvals, ensuring completion within 24 hours of request submission.

#### 3.5.2 Functional Requirements

**FR-040: Payment Request**
```markdown
- **Priority**: High
- **Description**: Attorneys shall submit compensation requests electronically
- **Inputs**: Hours worked, expenses, case information
- **Processing**: Validate against case records and rate schedules
- **Outputs**: Payment request record, validation results
```

**FR-041: Payment Approval**
```markdown
- **Priority**: High
- **Description**: OAA staff shall review and approve compensation requests
- **Inputs**: Payment requests, approval authority, budget constraints
- **Processing**: Verify eligibility, check limits, approve/deny with reasons
- **Outputs**: Approval decisions, payment records, denial explanations
```

### 3.6 Compliance Reporting

#### 3.6.1 Description
The system shall generate compliance reports required by the Texas Fair Defense Act.

#### 3.6.2 Functional Requirements

**FR-050: Report Generation**
```markdown
- **Priority**: High
- **Description**: Generate TFDA compliance reports on demand and scheduled basis
- **Inputs**: Case data, appointment records, contact logs, time metrics
- **Processing**: Aggregate data, calculate metrics, format according to state requirements
- **Outputs**: Compliance reports, exception summaries, performance metrics
```

## 4 External Interface Requirements

### 4.1 Software Interfaces

**SI-001: Court Case Management System**
```markdown
- **Interface Type**: REST API / Web Services
- **Purpose**: Exchange case data and custody status information
- **Data Elements**: Case numbers, defendant information, hearing dates, custody status
- **Frequency**: Real-time for critical updates, batch for data synchronization
```

**SI-002: District Attorney Electronic Case Filing System**
```markdown
- **Interface Type**: REST API / Web Services
- **Purpose**: Coordinate charge filings and case decisions
- **Data Elements**: Charge information, filing decisions, case dispositions
- **Frequency**: Real-time updates as filings occur
```

**SI-003: External Accounting Systems**
```markdown
- **Interface Type**: Batch File Transfer / API
- **Purpose**: Process compensation payments
- **Data Elements**: Payment amounts, attorney information, approval data
- **Frequency**: Daily batch processing
```

### 4.2 Hardware Interfaces
- Standard web browser interface accessible via county network
- No specialized hardware requirements beyond standard county workstations

### 4.3 Communications Interfaces
- HTTPS for all web communications
- Email notifications for status updates and alerts
- System-to-system web services for integration points

## 5 Non-Functional Requirements

### 5.1 Performance Requirements

**PER-001: Processing Time**
```markdown
- **Requirement**: All counsel requests shall be processed within 24 hours of submission
- **Measurement**: Time from request submission to attorney assignment
- **Target**: 100% compliance with 24-hour window
```

**PER-002: Contact Confirmation**
```markdown
- **Requirement**: First attorney contact shall be confirmed within 1 working day of appointment
- **Measurement**: Time from appointment to contact confirmation
- **Target**: 95% compliance with 1-working-day requirement
```

**PER-003: Compensation Processing**
```markdown
- **Requirement**: Compensation approvals shall be completed within 24 hours of request
- **Measurement**: Time from payment request submission to approval decision
- **Target**: 100% compliance with 24-hour window
```

### 5.2 Security Requirements

**SEC-001: Data Protection**
```markdown
- **Requirement**: All sensitive defendant data shall be encrypted in transit and at rest
- **Standard**: Compliance with Texas DITR security guidelines
- **Implementation**: AES-256 encryption for data at rest, TLS 1.2+ for data in transit
```

**SEC-002: Access Control**
```markdown
- **Requirement**: Role-based access control with least privilege principles
- **Implementation**: User authentication via county Active Directory, role-based permissions
```

### 5.3 Compliance Requirements

**COM-001: Legal Compliance**
```markdown
- **Requirement**: All electronic transactions shall comply with Texas UETA
- **Verification**: Legal review of transaction processes and records
```

**COM-002: Reporting Compliance**
```markdown
- **Requirement**: Reporting shall meet Texas Fair Defense Act compliance metrics
- **Verification**: Validation against TFDA reporting requirements
```

### 5.4 Reliability Requirements
- System availability: 99.5% during business hours (7:00 AM - 7:00 PM CT)
- Data backup: Daily incremental, weekly full backups
- Recovery time objective: 4 hours for critical system restoration

## 6 Constraints, Assumptions & Dependencies

### 6.1 Legal Constraints
- Must comply with Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Articles 1.051, 15.17, 26.04–26.052
- Must adhere to Texas Fair Defense Act requirements
- Must maintain compliance with Texas UETA for electronic records

### 6.2 Technical Constraints
- Must integrate with existing Court Case Management System architecture
- Must maintain compatibility with DA Electronic Case Filing System interfaces
- Must use county-standard security and authentication protocols

### 6.3 Assumptions
- Existing Court Case Management System provides accurate case data
- External systems maintain required availability and performance levels
- Users have adequate training and system access

### 6.4 Dependencies
- Successful integration with Court Case Management System
- Availability of DA Electronic Case Filing System interfaces
- County network infrastructure supporting system requirements

## 7 Acceptance Criteria

### 7.1 Legal Compliance Acceptance
- All system processes demonstrate compliance with Texas CCP Articles 1.051, 15.17, 26.04–26.052
- Reporting functionality meets all Texas Fair Defense Act requirements
- Electronic transactions comply with Texas UETA and DITR guidelines

### 7.2 Performance Acceptance
- 100% of test counsel requests processed within 24-hour window
- 95% of test attorney contacts confirmed within 1 working day
- 100% of test compensation approvals completed within 24 hours

### 7.3 Integration Acceptance
- Successful bidirectional data exchange with Court Case Management System
- Reliable interface functionality with DA Electronic Case Filing System
- Accurate data transfer to external accounting systems

### 7.4 User Acceptance
- All user roles can complete assigned tasks efficiently
- System interfaces are intuitive and require minimal training
- Reporting functions meet operational needs of all stakeholder groups
